title: The Spark Risk Council can stop a proposal before token holders ever vote on it
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4 establishes the Spark Risk Council as a body that "safeguards the integrity and security of the Spark Ecosystem by conducting pre-vote risk reviews and, where necessary, **preventing proposals from proceeding to a vote**." The effect clause is blunt: on a Failed SRC Review, "the proposal does not proceed to Snapshot (or is withdrawn)" (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.4.5).

The placement matters more than the power. A risk body that publishes an analysis and lets holders decide is an information provider; one that decides what holders may decide on is a gate. Spark chose the second, and the mandate at A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.1 names both functions in sequence — inform the community, *and* where necessary prevent.

The justification is that some proposals are unsafe to put to a vote at all. A malicious proposal that reaches Snapshot can pass through voter apathy, low turnout, or a whale acting in bad faith; once it passes, the damage is executed. Screening before the vote removes the possibility that a governance attack succeeds through legitimate machinery.

The cost is a hard ceiling on token-holder sovereignty. Three appointed seats decide by majority (A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.4.2) what the entire SPK electorate is permitted to consider, and the Artifact provides no override — no supermajority bypass, no appeal to holders. Every other constraint on the SRC in this section exists to make that ceiling tolerable.
description: A Failed SRC Review determination keeps a proposal off Snapshot entirely, so the risk check is a gate in front of the electorate rather than advice delivered to it.
